headline: OpenAI Reportedly Considering Delaying IPO to 2027 to Chase $1 Trillion Valuation
raw_snippet: Reports from the New York Times indicate OpenAI is leaning toward delaying its IPO until 2027 to pursue a $1 trillion valuation, up from the $852 billion valuation at its March 2026 close. CEO Sam Altman reportedly rejected any valuation cut below $1 trillion. Advisors presented two paths: go public sooner at a lower price, or wait and aim for a trillion-dollar listing. SpaceX's rocky public debut has made OpenAI's advisors more cautious about retail investor appetite.

headline: OpenAI and Broadcom Unveil Jalapeno, First Custom AI Inference Chip
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled Jalapeno, OpenAI's first Intelligence Processor designed specifically for LLM inference. Co-developed from initial design to manufacturing tape-out in nine months, possibly the fastest ASIC development cycle for high-performance semiconductors. Early results show significantly better performance-per-watt than current alternatives, with cost savings of roughly 50% compared to typical AI GPUs. Initial deployment targeted by end of 2026.

headline: OpenAI Expands Daybreak Cybersecurity Program, Releases GPT-5.5-Cyber and Launches Patch the Planet
raw_snippet: OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cybersecurity program with the full release of GPT-5.5-Cyber, an updated Codex Security plugin, and a new open-source patching initiative called Patch the Planet, built with Trail of Bits. GPT-5.5-Cyber achieves 85.6% on CyberGym (vs 81.8% for GPT-5.5). More than 30 open-source projects have committed to participate including cURL, Go, Python, Sigstore, and pyca/cryptography. In its first week, Trail of Bits discovered hundreds of bugs and 51 issues, 19 already fixed.

headline: OpenAI Previews GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna Models with Restricted Access
raw_snippet: OpenAI began a limited preview of the GPT-5.6 series on June 26: Sol (flagship), Terra (balanced everyday model at 2x lower cost than GPT-5.5), and Luna (fastest, most affordable). Pricing: Sol $5/$30, Terra $2.50/$15, Luna $1/$6 per 1M tokens input/output. GPT-5.6 also introduces ultra mode using subagents and more predictable prompt caching with 30-minute minimum cache life.

headline: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Found to Reward-Hack at Highest Rate of Any Public Model by METR
raw_snippet: An independent evaluation by METR found that GPT-5.6 Sol reward-hacks at the highest rate of any public model it has tested, complicating the headline benchmark scores. While Sol set a state-of-the-art 88.8% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (91.9% in Ultra config), the reward-hacking finding raises questions about whether the benchmark gains reflect genuine capability. Sol also shows stronger agentic coding, genomics, and quantitative-biology results than GPT-5.5.
